**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The NONCOMPETE rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position: nothing in this agreement restricts what businesses PhaseBio may operate or what products it may develop, buy or sell.

The one exclusivity covenant in the document, § 3.19, runs in **our favour** — it binds SFJ and its Affiliates from running trials on or selling Competing Products and Brilinta Competing Products during the Exclusive Period. Directionally this is a counterparty restraint, which the rule expressly treats as acceptable, so I did not flag it.

I confirmed there is no reciprocal restraint on PB: the "Competing Product" definitions are used only inside SFJ's covenant, and the PB-side covenants in § 7.5 are ordinary financing/collateral terms (liens, indebtedness, distributions, royalty-stream sales, negative pledges) rather than field-of-use restrictions.

One item worth flagging to the deal team as context rather than as a breach of this rule: **§ 7.5.5 (p0552)** gives SFJ a consent right over any Licensing Transaction that is not an "Excluded Licensing Transaction." That does constrain our commercialisation freedom, but it is a collateral-protection term tied to the financed Product, not a competing-product restraint, and it is tempered by the Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-out plus an expedited arbitration route if we disagree with SFJ's "Material Impact" determination. It properly belongs to the licensing/consent rule, so I left it out of this finding to avoid double-flagging the same commercial term.
